map: D defines fixed components (58) from independent Haar n-frames, sources v_j=n^{-1/2}sum_i w_ij, clock C_v, radial protection J and affine dual coupling over one ball. D.1 proves uniform individual smoothness and gap O(Mq), q=sqrt(n)/R. D.2-D.4 force source recovery at a small Moreau gradient.

D.4 couples exact values/full gradients to an ideal censored transcript until a constant fraction of frame rows is disclosed. Normalized queries and output cover arbitrary norms and unqueried outputs. D.5 gives Omega(Mn). Scaling caps R at n^{1/4}, handles insufficient gap using independent Omega(n), and uses the smooth baseline for bounded B and small n, yielding the first branch.

E.1-E.4 define stronger simultaneous forward/transpose branch rounds with source releases. E.3 proves pathwise p_t(K)<=min{1,rho^{-r_K}binom(K,t)/n^t}, charging releases and cached probes chronologically. E.5-E.8 provide fixed product-Haar coupling and the Gaussian nuisance reservoir.

E.12 computes exact quadratic endpoint energy and radius O(n^{1/4}N). E.13 first controls connectors for the constrained ball. The outer assembly (99), E.15 admissibility, and E.16-E.19 single-frontier certificate then put the unconstrained optimizer inside the prescribed ball; this avoids circular dual-interiority reasoning.

E.10 converts a Moreau output to terminal correlation using analytic prox displacement, and verifies exact inactive first jets for unreleased nonlinear terms. E.23 simulates each component value/full-gradient query by one stronger matrix round with finitely many marked channels. E.24 gives Omega(nM(N-1)) for a static seed-independent law. E.11 scales M proportional to A and N proportional to B/n^{1/4}; this high-diameter interface alone requires B>=B_hd n^{1/4}.

F.1 explicitly imports Peng, Tang and Jia [6], Theorem 3.1 with Appendix G.1 Oracle conventions. Its local transfer uses direct-gradient tolerance 3epsilon/2, handles small n through constant-size simulation and supplies additive n by a hidden-component quadratic. The external original was not read.

proofs.full_local_argument: Given 1<=s<=n individually L/2-smooth components g_j, partition [n] into public groups of sizes r_j=floor(n/s) or ceil(n/s), and define f_i=n g_j/(s r_j) for i in group j. Since (n/s)/floor(n/s)<=2, every f_i is L-smooth. Summing gives n^{-1}sum_i f_i=s^{-1}sum_j g_j. Thus the value, average concavity, gap and domain are unchanged. One f_i query is exactly one g_j query multiplied by n/(s r_j), preserving adaptive transcripts, seeds, caps and outputs. The common value is L/2-weakly convex. For continuous bounded-below rho-weakly convex F, 0<lambda<=nu and rho nu<1, convexity of F+rho||.||^2/2 gives <a-b,u-v>>=-rho||u-v||^2 for subgradients a,b. At u=P_nu(x),v=P_nu(y), take a=(x-u)/nu,b=(y-v)/nu to obtain (1-rho nu)||u-v||^2<=<x-y,u-v>. Hence P_nu is 1/(1-rho nu)-Lipschitz. Put p=P_lambda(x),g=(x-p)/lambda. Proximal optimality gives p=P_nu(p+nu g). Consequently ||P_nu(x)-p||<=(nu-lambda)||g||/(1-rho nu), and ||grad F_nu(x)||<=((1-rho lambda)/(1-rho nu))||grad F_lambda(x)||. At rho=L/2,lambda=1/(2L),nu=1/L the factor is 3/2. Import E.1's interface c_hd A_g s^{3/4}B_g for A_g>=A_hd and B_g>=B_hd s^{1/4}, taking B_hd>=1. Set b_*=3B_hd. For B>=b_*, let X=min{n,(B/b_*)^4} and s=floor(X); then 1<=s<=n and s>=X/2. Choose L_g=L/2 and epsilon_g=3epsilon/2, so A_g=2A/9,B_g=B/3. For A>=max{9A_hd/2,A_sm}, the interface applies. Replication and the transfer yield T_IS>=(2c_hd/27)A B s^{3/4}. Moreover B s^{3/4}>=2^{-3/4}b_*^{-3}min{n^{3/4}B,B^4}. Combine this and independent T_IS>=c_sm n using max(u,v)>=(u+v)/2. If 0<=B<b_*, then min{B^4,n^{3/4}B}<=b_*^4 sqrt(n); the full smooth baseline c_sm(n+A sqrt(n)) gives the desired inequality after decreasing a universal constant. Boundaries n=1 and X=1 are included. Different families justify the maximum without a common assembled instance.

assumptions: Every component joint gradient is L-Lipschitz on R^{d_x} x Y. The average, but not necessarily every component, is concave in y. Phi is bounded below with initial gap at most Delta.

Queries choose arbitrary i and feasible (x,y), returning exact component value and full joint gradient. Repeated/adaptive indices, arbitrary query norms, private randomness, full transcript dependence and unqueried outputs are covered. Computation/memory and known-domain projection are free; exact unknown max/prox and Moreau-gradient evaluation are not supplied. No uniform component affine-gradient bound is assumed.
statement.conclusion: T_IS>=c[n+A min{sqrt(n)Bbar,n^{3/4}}] and T_IS>=c[n+A min{B^4,n^{3/4}B}]. These lower bounds also hold for T_AS because IS(L) is a subclass of AS(L). The first branch retains Bbar; the second uses B. At D_Y=0 its nonlinear term vanishes, while the independent smooth baseline still gives n+A sqrt(n).
statement.objects_and_definitions: Euclidean primal space R^{d_x}; known nonempty compact convex Y subset R^{d_y} of diameter at most D_Y. Differentiable components on a neighborhood of the product; f=n^{-1}sum_i f_i, Phi=max_Y f. Define A=L Delta/epsilon^2, B=L D_Y/epsilon, Bbar=max(1,B). Phi_{1/(2L)}(c)=min_x{Phi(x)+L||x-c||^2}. T_IS is the least worst-case deterministic cap on exact component queries achieving P(||grad Phi_{1/(2L)}(xhat)||<=epsilon)>=2/3 on every IS instance.
statement.parameter_domains: n integer >=1; L,Delta,epsilon>0; D_Y>=0; A>=A_0. No additional n- or B-dependent accuracy restriction. Hard dimensions are finite but can grow with parameters and exponentially with the serial edge count.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: There exist universal A_0,c>0 valid for every admissible parameter tuple. For every insufficient-fixed-budget measurable randomized adaptive algorithm, some fixed admissible finite-dimensional instance and known hard domain violates its 2/3 guarantee. Hard distributions are independent of the private seed. The two inequalities are separate minimax assertions and may use different families. Domain hardness is existential over known admissible domains, not universal over all shapes of the same diameter.
